title: Files, Folders, File Extensions and Paths in Web Projects
learningObjectives: Explain files, directories, project roots and nested folder structures, and describe how a browser-based project is organized.
Identify common web file types including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON, SVG, raster images, fonts and media, and explain the usual role of each.
Distinguish a filename extension from the actual content type and explain why servers use MIME types when delivering web resources.
Read a project tree and derive a resource path from the location of the referring document.
Resolve relative URLs using the current document URL, path segments, dot segments and the effect of a base element.
Distinguish document-relative paths, root-relative paths, absolute URLs and operating-system file-system paths.
Explain the difference between URL path separators and platform-specific file-system path separators, and avoid copying local disk paths into web URLs.
Diagnose path failures caused by spelling, letter case, extension mismatch, incorrect nesting, URL encoding and deployment base paths.
Organize a maintainable front-end project using predictable folders for pages, styles, scripts, assets and data.
Apply safe naming and resource-handling practices, including avoiding secrets in public assets and avoiding traversal or untrusted file-path assumptions in server code.

understand.concept: A web project is a collection of files arranged in directories. HTML files describe documents, CSS files describe presentation, JavaScript files provide behaviour, and assets such as images, fonts and JSON provide supporting resources. A path identifies where a resource is located. In a web page, a relative URL is resolved against a base URL—normally the document URL—not against the folder where the developer happens to be working in the editor. The browser requests a URL; the server maps that URL to a resource or application response.
understand.whyItMatters: Incorrect paths are a common reason that stylesheets, scripts, images and links fail after a project is moved or deployed. Understanding the difference between a local file-system path and a web URL is essential when moving from a single HTML file to a multi-page website or production deployment.
understand.history: Directory trees and filename extensions became common ways to organize files. The Web added URL-based resource addressing, which is related to but distinct from the paths used by a computer's operating system. Modern servers can map URLs to generated responses, so a URL does not always correspond directly to a physical file.
understand.analogy: A project directory is like a filing system: folders group related resources, filenames identify individual items, and a path describes how to locate one item from a known starting point.
understand.analogyLimit: A browser URL is not simply a copy of a computer's disk path. URL resolution follows URL rules, servers may route requests dynamically, and a resource's extension does not guarantee its content or MIME type.

explain.narrative: Consider a project with index.html at its root, styles/site.css, scripts/app.js and assets/logo.svg. From index.html, the relative URL styles/site.css enters the styles folder. From pages/about.html, the same stylesheet is one directory above and is referenced as ../styles/site.css. A root-relative URL such as /assets/logo.svg starts at the origin's root path; it is not the same as a path relative to the current page. An absolute URL includes a scheme and host, such as https://cdn.example.test/assets/logo.svg. The browser resolves relative references using the document's base URL, which can be affected by a base element. URL paths use forward slashes regardless of the developer's operating system. File-system paths such as C:\\projects\\site\\index.html or /home/dev/site/index.html are local operating-system locations and should not be copied into deployed HTML. Servers return resources with media types such as text/html, text/css, text/javascript, application/json or image/svg+xml; the browser uses response metadata and resource context when deciding how to process them.

examples.title: A maintainable project directory
examples.code:
my-site/
├── index.html
├── pages/
│   └── about.html
├── styles/
│   └── site.css
├── scripts/
│   └── app.js
└── assets/
    ├── logo.svg
    └── hero.webp
examples.explanation: The project root contains the main page and separate folders for pages, styles, scripts and static assets. A larger project may use additional folders for fonts, data, tests and build output.
examples.expectedOutput: A predictable directory structure that makes resource locations easy to identify.

examples.title: Resolve a path from the referring document
examples.code:
Document: my-site/index.html
Stylesheet: styles/site.css
Image: assets/logo.svg
Script: scripts/app.js

Document: my-site/pages/about.html
Stylesheet from about.html: ../styles/site.css
Image from about.html: ../assets/logo.svg
examples.explanation: A relative URL starts from the referring document's base URL. The .. segment moves to the parent path. Count folder levels from the page that contains the reference, not from the project root unless that is where the page lives.
examples.expectedOutput: Both pages can reference the same shared resources using different relative paths.

examples.title: Four path forms are not interchangeable
examples.code:
Relative URL:      ../styles/site.css
Root-relative URL: /styles/site.css
Absolute URL:      https://static.example.test/site.css
Local file path:   C:\\projects\\my-site\\styles\\site.css
examples.explanation: Relative and root-relative URLs are resolved within a web origin. An absolute URL names the scheme and host. A local file path identifies a location on a developer's computer and is not a portable web resource reference.
examples.expectedOutput: You can select a path form appropriate to the deployment and page location.

examples.title: The document base can change relative URL resolution
examples.explanation: The base element changes how relative URLs in the document are resolved. It should be used deliberately: it can affect links, scripts, images and stylesheets, not only the one resource shown here.
examples.expectedOutput: The relative stylesheet URL resolves against the declared base URL rather than the page's ordinary URL.

examples.title: File extension and HTTP media type
examples.code:
URL: /assets/app.js
Response header: Content-Type: text/javascript

URL: /data/catalog.json
Response header: Content-Type: application/json
examples.explanation: A .js or .json extension is a naming convention. The server's Content-Type response header communicates the media type. Incorrect MIME configuration can prevent some resources, especially module scripts, from loading as intended.
examples.expectedOutput: You can inspect both the requested URL and the response Content-Type when diagnosing a resource-loading problem.

practise.guidedTask: Use the project tree from the examples. Write the correct relative stylesheet and image URLs for index.html and pages/about.html. Then change the stylesheet reference in about.html to site.css and explain why the browser looks in the wrong directory.
practise.independentTask: Create the project tree locally. Add two HTML pages, one shared CSS file, one JavaScript file and one image. Link every resource from both pages. Test the project locally, then move it under a nested deployment path and identify which root-relative references would need adjustment. Use the Network panel to verify each request and response Content-Type.
hints: Start path resolution from the referring document's base URL, not from the editor's workspace root.
The .. segment moves one directory level upward; it does not mean the project root.
A root-relative URL begins at the origin root path. It may behave differently when an app is deployed below a subpath.
Use forward slashes in URLs. Operating-system file paths are not portable web URLs.
Check letter case and exact spelling. A path that works on a case-insensitive computer can fail on a case-sensitive server.
Inspect the Network panel for the actual request URL, status code, redirect chain and Content-Type response header.
A base element changes relative URL resolution across the document. Do not add it casually.
Never place passwords, private keys, service credentials or other secrets in public project assets.

questions.prompt: From pages/about.html, which relative URL points to the shared styles/site.css file at the project root?
questions.explanation: about.html is inside pages, so one .. segment moves to the project root before entering styles.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a root-relative URL and a local file-system path?
options: A root-relative URL starts at a web origin's root path; a local file path identifies a location on a particular computer.
A local file path always starts with https://.
questions.answer: A root-relative URL starts at a web origin's root path; a local file path identifies a location on a particular computer.
questions.explanation: Web URL resolution and operating-system file-system path rules are different. A local disk path is not a portable resource URL.

questions.prompt: What normally determines the base used to resolve a relative URL in a document?
options: The document's base URL, normally derived from its URL and possibly affected by a base element.
questions.answer: The document's base URL, normally derived from its URL and possibly affected by a base element.
questions.explanation: Relative URLs are resolved against the document base URL. A base element can deliberately change that base.

questions.prompt: Why should a developer inspect Content-Type when a script fails to load?
options: The response media type can affect how the browser processes the resource and whether module scripts are accepted.
Content-Type determines the folder colour in the editor.
Content-Type is the same as the URL fragment.
questions.answer: The response media type can affect how the browser processes the resource and whether module scripts are accepted.
questions.explanation: The server should return an appropriate media type. Incorrect MIME configuration can cause resource-loading or module-script errors.
